walkthroughs.body_html:
The signature shape of Classical first movements. The exposition states two themes (Theme 1 in tonic, Theme 2 in dominant). The development takes those themes through new keys.

The recapitulation brings both themes back in the tonic key — a satisfying return home.

A concerto pits a soloist against the orchestra in (usually) three movements: fast-slow-fast. Listen for the cadenza near the end of the first movement.

A symphony is for full orchestra alone, normally four movements: fast – slow – minuet/scherzo – fast finale.

The orchestra has four families: strings, woodwind, brass, percussion. Tutti means everyone plays; solo means just one. Antiphonal textures pass material between groups (like call-and-response).

A composer's choice of texture creates contrast and drama throughout the movement.
